newsitem.title: POLAND: BOXING-GOLOTA IN POLISH COURT OVER BRAWL YEARS AGO.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-GOLOTA IN POLISH COURT OVER BRAWL YEARS AGO.

text.p: Heavyweight Andrzej Golota, who last year twice squandered likely victories against U.S. rival Riddick Bowe by landing low blows, on Tuesday faced a court in his native Poland over a brawl seven years ago.

Golota, 28, has returned to Poland after receiving a letter from Polish authorities, promising he would not face instant arrest, so he could settle the case which has long prevented him from coming home.
PAP news agency said he was accused of beating a stranger, Pawel Bialostocki, and robbing him of his shirt and trousers in a restaurant in Wloclawek, central Poland.
It said the boxer apologised to Bialostocki, and expressed regret for the events, saying: "Now I feel disgust over them."
He suggested that he had already reached a financial deal with the offended man, it added.

After local prosecutors accused him of robbery and using a dangerous instrument, he left the country, where he has since been wanted by police, but applied last year for a chance to clear the matter up.
The hearing is due to continue on Wednesday in Wloclawek, where the courthouse was surrounded by hundreds of Golota's local admirers.
